finalText:
It's a small Node HTTP service, five files, no dependencies. Here's how a request flows.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[server.js] -->|checks Bearer token| B[auth.js]
  A -->|passes user + req| C[routes.js]
  C -->|reads| D[cache.js]
  D -->|misses fall through to| E[store.js]
  C -->|writes go straight to| E
```

- **`server.js`** — the entry point. Starts an HTTP server, checks every request's token, then hands it off.
- **`auth.js`** — checks Bearer tokens shaped `<userId>.<signature>`, signed with HMAC-SHA256 from `AUTH_SECRET`.
- **`routes.js`** — a small table mapping `METHOD /path` to a handler. Three routes exist: get a user, list orders, add an order.
- **`cache.js`** — a 256-entry LRU sitting in front of reads. No expiry of its own.
- **`store.js`** — the actual data, kept in memory, each record expiring 15 minutes after it's last written. Nothing here yet persists to disk, so a restart wipes everything.

One thing worth knowing early: writes (`POST /orders`) go straight to the store and don't touch the cache, so a cached `orders:<id>` list can go stale until it falls out of the LRU or the 15-minute TTL clears it.
